ai.description: *Minervarya nepalensis* is a small frog (25–35 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale vertebral stripe. It features prominent, broken longitudinal skin ridges and a distinct dark triangular snout mark.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya nepalensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and well-developed glandular fold along the dorsolateral region of its back.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya nepalensis* inhabits moist, subtropical to temperate forests and agricultural fields, typically found at elevations between 800 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nepal Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt for small insects and invertebrates near streams and moist forest habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya nepalensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying large clutches of eggs in stagnant or slow-moving water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya nepalensis* is found in the Himalayan foothills of Nepal and northern India, typically inhabiting elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nepal Wart Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "chirp" or "click" notes, typically heard from shallow pools or wet grassy areas near streams.
